chapter: National Guard band and first jobs in Chicago
title: Cecil Irwin, Morehouse and Wilberforce
summary: Caldwell and Cecil Irwin planned to attend college together but parents sent Irwin to Morehouse and Caldwell to Wilberforce.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: And when we graduated from grammar school and from high school, we were always supposed to go to Atlanta, Georgia, to go to the Morehouse University because they had a big, beautiful -- they had a mixed curriculum there for students. And he went to Morehouse, and I went to Wilberforce. So they could --
Yeah, Cecil Irwin (unintelligible) went to Morehouse, and I went to Wilberforce -- Wilberforce University.

Well, we all had decided to go one place together, but then, you know, parents, they have something to do with where you're going to go anyway, so when we finished high school, he went to Morehouse, and I went to Wilberforce.
Well, I mean he -- Cecil Irwin, he must have got -- I mean he was really very advanced, wasn't he, as an arranger and everything?
Yeah, was a very fine clarinet player, just same as Simon (unintelligible) because we all stuck, the three guys, we three just -- one without the other. We all just stuck together.
